narrative.title: Merging Two Sorted Audit Streams
narrative.scenario: Two replicas each keep their own sorted stream of audit event ids, and a compliance job needs the combined set of distinct ids. Both streams are long enough that concatenating and re-sorting would be wasteful, so the merge should walk them side by side and emit each id exactly once.
narrative.inputFormat: Two sorted arrays arr1 and arr2 with sizes n and m respectively.
narrative.outputFormat: A sorted array containing every distinct value that appears in either input.
constraints: arr1 and arr2 are each sorted in non-decreasing order

testCases.explanation: Every id of the shorter stream already appears in the longer one, so the union is just the longer stream.
Repeated ids inside each stream are collapsed, and shared ids are emitted once.

hintLevels: Level 1: Both streams are sorted, so the next smallest unused id is always at the head of one of the two pointers.
Level 2: Compare the values under both pointers, emit the smaller (or either one when equal) and advance past the emitted value.
Level 3: After one stream runs out, the other still holds ids - and when both pointers point at the same value, advancing only one of them duplicates that id.
